requirements.title: Run a reconcile every few packages and at the end
requirements.rationale: A list that is only corrected at the end is out of date for the whole run.

criteria.condition: the number of packages landed since the last reconcile reaches `--reconcile-every`, 5 when the flag is absent
criteria.action: run a reconcile step before the next package
criteria.contract: the reconcile's session starts after that package's landing and before the next package's session; the count in the state file returns to 0

setup: the fixture repository, the fake claude and the in-memory issuex client of internal/specrun's helpers
check.pseudocode: in internal/specrun/reconcile_test.go (new), a table over --reconcile-every {1, 2, 5} with five open packages: assert the order of the sessions started, by their prompts: with 2 -> 01, 02, reconcile, 03, 04, reconcile, 05, reconcile; with 5 -> five packages then one reconcile; with 1 -> a reconcile after each and none added at the end

criteria.condition: every package is done and a package has landed since the last reconcile, or no reconcile is recorded in the ledger
criteria.action: run one reconcile step before ending
criteria.contract: the last session of the run is a reconcile; when the last step was a reconcile and no package landed since, no session starts and the run ends with `all_done`

criteria.action: take the number of packages between reconciles from it, `0` meaning only the reconcile at the end, with `SPECRUN_RECONCILE_EVERY` as its default when set
criteria.contract: a negative number or a value that is no integer is a usage error with exit code 2 naming the flag or the variable; with `0` and five packages the only reconcile is the last session

check.pseudocode: in internal/specrun/flags_test.go, beside the existing flag tables: {absent -> 5; 3 -> 3; 0 -> 0; SPECRUN_RECONCILE_EVERY=2 -> 2; -1 -> exit code 2; 'often' -> exit code 2}; in internal/specrun/reconcile_test.go one case with 0 and five packages: the session order is the five packages, then reconcile

criteria.condition: `specrun` is started and its state records the count of packages since the last reconcile, or a reconcile step as running
criteria.action: continue from that count, and run a reconcile recorded as running again
criteria.contract: with `--reconcile-every 2`, one package landed before the restart and one after it, the reconcile follows the second; a running reconcile is the first session after the restart

requirements.title: Hand the session the issues it may adopt, and nothing else
requirements.rationale: A reconcile that could touch any issue would sooner or later relabel one a person opened.

criteria.action: select the open issues that carry no label starting with `af:` and whose title starts with the directory name of a package under the spec root or its archive followed by a colon, write them to `<step>-adopt.json` in the log directory, and start the session
criteria.contract: the file is a JSON array of `{number, title, url, package}`, `[]` when none is selected; the session's prompt is `/af-impl --reconcile <adopt file> --report <log dir>/<step>-report.md`, with the flags, the stall rule and the stream files of every session

criteria.condition: the reconcile session ends and the base branch is not checked out, the working tree is not clean, or `HEAD` is not the commit it was before the step
criteria.contract: exit code 1; `result.stopped.reason` names the check; the ledger line has outcome `stopped`; no rule is applied to the forge and no further session starts

criteria.condition: the reconcile session ends and the report file does not exist
criteria.contract: `warnings` holds one `reconcile_report_missing` entry naming the path; the rules run and the ledger line has outcome `reconciled`

requirements.title: Settle by rule what needs no judgement, after the session
requirements.rationale: Labels, the dependency graph and git decide these; a rule applies them the same way every time, at no model cost.

criteria.condition: a reconcile session has passed its checks and an issue from the adopt file is still open with no kind label
criteria.action: add `af:deviation` and `af:from-<NN>` of the package its title names, and comment on it
criteria.contract: the issue carries both labels and one comment naming the rule `adoption-unsettled` and the commit of the base branch; an adopted issue that has a kind is left to the other label rules

criteria.condition: a reconcile session has passed its checks and an open issue carries `af:deviation` and `af:accepted` and not `af:rejected`
criteria.action: close the issue with a comment naming the ADR the issue cites
criteria.contract: the issue is closed; the comment names the rule `deviation-accepted`, the commit of the base branch and the first path `docs/adr/<file>.md` in the issue's body, or says that the issue cites no ADR

criteria.condition: a reconcile session has passed its checks and an open issue carries `af:deviation` and `af:rejected` and not `af:accepted`
criteria.action: remove `af:deviation` and `af:rejected`, add `af:defect` and `af:severity-correctness`, and comment that a person rejected the deviation
criteria.contract: the issue is open with `af:defect`, `af:severity-correctness` and its `af:from-<NN>`; the comment names the rule `deviation-rejected` and the commit of the base branch

criteria.condition: an open issue carries `af:accepted` and `af:rejected` together
criteria.action: leave the issue as it is and warn
criteria.contract: the forge records no write for it; `warnings` holds one `deviation_conflict` entry naming the issue

criteria.condition: the rules of a reconcile have been applied
criteria.action: apply the label rules `incomplete-labels` and `awaits-finished` to every open `af:` issue, write the ledger line, and list the open deviations that carry neither `af:accepted` nor `af:rejected`, oldest first
criteria.contract: the ledger line has kind `reconcile`, outcome `reconciled` and the numbers `adopted`, `closed` and `settled`: issues from the adopt file that now carry a kind, issues open before the step and closed after it, and deviations accepted or rejected; `result.open_deviations` lists number, title, URL and creation time, oldest first, and stderr prints the same

requirements.title: Show the reconcile in a dry run
requirements.rationale: The reconcile writes to many issues at once; a person should be able to see the list first.

criteria.condition: `--dry-run` is given and a forge client can be made
criteria.action: say when the next step is a reconcile, list the issues it would hand over for adoption, and add the deviation changes to what the label rules would change
criteria.contract: `result.next_step.kind` is `reconcile` when one is due; `result.would_adopt` lists the selected issues; `result.would_change` holds an entry with rule `deviation-accepted` or `deviation-rejected` for each labelled deviation; the forge records no write and no file is written

execution_paths.title: specrun reconciles after a package: an old issue is adopted, a resolved one closed, an accepted deviation settled

steps.action: adds `af:accepted` to a deviation issue and runs `specrun --reconcile-every 1`
runs the session for the next package and checks the landing
starts a reconcile: selects the unlabelled issue titled after a package, writes the adopt file and starts the reconcile session
labels the adopted issue with its kind and origin, closes an issue whose closing condition holds on the base branch, and writes the report
checks that the repository is as it was, applies the label rules, closes the accepted deviation with a comment naming its ADR
writes the reconcile's ledger line and lists the deviations still open

real_components: the fake claude as a real process
the reconcile rules against the in-memory issuex client
the adopt file, the report and the ledger on disk
setup: the fixture repository, the fake claude and the in-memory issuex client of internal/specrun's helpers

one open package; on the forge an unlabelled open issue '00_zero: no caller', an open af:awaits issue, an open af:deviation + af:accepted issue citing docs/adr/03-x.md, and an open af:deviation issue; a fake reconcile session that labels the first, closes the second and writes the report
end_state: the sessions started are the package, then a reconcile whose prompt names the adopt file and the report
the adopted issue carries the kind the session gave it and got no write from specrun
the accepted deviation is closed with a comment containing docs/adr/03-x.md
the ledger's last line is a reconcile with adopted 1, closed 2, settled 1
the result lists one open deviation and exit code is 0
smoke.pseudocode: in cmd/specrun/main_test.go, beside the existing end-to-end tests: code = Main(['--reconcile-every', '1']); assert code == 0; assert prompts == ['/af-impl .specs/01_…', '/af-impl --reconcile … --report …']; assert the adopt file lists one issue; assert state(accepted deviation) == 'closed'; l = last(ledger); assert l.kind == 'reconcile' and l.adopted == 1 and l.closed == 2 and l.settled == 1; assert len(env.result.open_deviations) == 1
